task.name: A dev invocation started right after a gate failure is killed before producing output, consuming a retry for work that never ran
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

A dev invocation started immediately after a gate failure is killed before it
produces any output. Three occurrences, all on issue-2681, all the same shape:

| gate event | dev starts | dev dies | recorded |
|---|---|---|---|
| VALIDATE timeout 10:42:41 (2026-08-30) | 10:42:42 | 10:42:53 | `exit=-9`, `$0.000`, `output=0 chars` |
| VALIDATE timeout 00:17:53 | 00:17:54 | 00:18:07 | `exit=-9`, `$0.000`, `output=0 chars` |
| VALIDATE FAIL 14:41:19 (2026-08-31) | 14:41:20 | 14:41:31 | `exit=-9`, `$0.000`, `output=0 chars` |

Run `0b14b21993ac` records the third:

```
14:41:20 ▸ DEV opus iter=2
14:41:20   Starting anthropic-opus-cli (model=opus, timeout=3600s)...
14:41:31   ⚠ 3 process(es) started by this invocation outlived it in their own
           process group(s) (pids=[27400, 27402, 27403]); killing them directly
14:41:31   ... anthropic-opus-cli done (11s)
14:41:31   [DEV] FAIL | exit=-9 | cost=$0.000 | output=0 chars
```

The story then aborts as a shared-infrastructure failure with no judgment
obtained, which is the correct report — the classification fix from #2807 is
working. What is not addressed is that the invocation is killed at all: the
iteration produces nothing, costs nothing, and the retry budget is consumed.

In the same run, the preceding iteration had backgrounded a long command and
returned while it was still running:

```
14:38:31 ↳ Bash: (make dev-check > /tmp/dc3.log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?" >> /tmp/dc3.log)
14:38:34 ↳ Bash: until grep -q "EXIT=" /tmp/dc3.log; do sleep 30; done; echo DONE
14:38:42   [DEV] OK | exit=0 | cost=$1.859 | output=81 chars
```

By contrast, a story whose dev delegated gate execution to the coordinator rather
than backgrounding it (issue-631, 2026-08-30) ran its post-gate-failure iterations
to completion.

## Expected behavior

An agent invocation is not terminated by cleanup belonging to work that preceded
it. Whatever a prior iteration leaves running is the prior iteration's to reap, and
reaping it does not reach a process started afterwards.

Where an invocation is nevertheless killed by the system rather than by its own
failure, that is distinguishable in the record from an agent that ran and produced
nothing, and it does not consume the story's retry budget — a retry that never
executed is not evidence about the story, and spending an allowance on it converts
an infrastructure fault into an exhausted story.


## Diagnosis

Two `forge diagnose` runs were attempted and neither reached a cause. Both spent
their full 600-second budget still investigating and were cut off, so the cause
below is recorded as not yet identified rather than guessed at.

- **Observed symptom:** a dev invocation started immediately after a gate failure
  is killed before producing any output, recording `exit=-9`, `$0.000` and
  `output=0 chars`, and the story's retry allowance is spent on an iteration that
  never ran.
- **Evidence:** three occurrences, all on issue-2681, all 11–13 seconds from start
  to death, each beginning within a second of a gate failure — VALIDATE timeout
  10:42:41 (2026-08-30) → dead 10:42:53; VALIDATE timeout 00:17:53 → dead
  00:18:07; VALIDATE FAIL 14:41:19 (2026-08-31) → dead 14:41:31. Run
  `0b14b21993ac` records the third alongside
  `⚠ 3 process(es) started by this invocation outlived it in their own process
  group(s) (pids=[27400, 27402, 27403]); killing them directly` at the moment of
  death. In that same run the preceding iteration had backgrounded `make dev-check`
  and returned in 20 seconds while it was still running, whereas issue-631's
  post-gate-failure iterations, whose dev delegated gate execution to the
  coordinator, ran to completion.
  A fourth occurrence appeared on a different agent path entirely: `forge diagnose`
  run `431dfd5c8643` against this issue ended with its full artifact reading
  `CLAUDE_STREAM_NO_TEXT: reason=missing_result_event`, and run `a7b1dffca825`
  logged `diagnose ended without a result event with no priceable stream usage`.
  So the failure is not confined to a dev invocation following a gate failure.
- **Ruled out:** operator interruption, and leftover processes from earlier runs as
  a standing precondition — the host had no matching process group and zero zombies
  when checked between occurrences.
- **Confirmed cause:** not yet identified. Two diagnose attempts exhausted a
  600-second budget each while still reading the referenced run artifacts; run
  `a7b1dffca825`'s output ends mid-investigation on
  `"Let me check the per-story audit and full log for more detail on the DEV phase
  teardown fields and the preceding iteration."`
- **Affected code path:** not yet established. The teardown message at the moment
  of death is emitted by the agent-invocation process-group supervision, which is
  where an investigation should start.
- **Fix-success criterion:** an agent invocation is not terminated by cleanup
  belonging to work that preceded it; where the system does terminate one, that is
  distinguishable in the record from an agent that ran and produced nothing, and it
  does not consume the story's retry allowance.

handoff.summary: Confirmed the undiagnosed cause by reproducing it with a new fake-CLI mode (silent_stdout_close): when the CLI's stdout reaches EOF with no stream events, _run_claude waits out _EXIT_GRACE_SECONDS (10s) and then SIGKILLs its own process group, producing exit=-9/$0.000/0 chars in ~11s. This matches all three DEV occurrences and the fourth forge diagnose occurrence (CLAUDE_STREAM_NO_TEXT: reason=missing_result_event), so all four share one mechanism. The kill is forge's own runner supervision, not cleanup belonging to the preceding iteration. Added FAILURE_KILLED_BEFORE_OUTPUT with a shared killed_before_output() predicate applied in all three CLI runners, discriminating on signal-exit plus zero execution artifacts (timeout/stuck/cancellation return coded results before it). The classified result carries a measured cost_usd=0.0 instead of None, which is precisely what lets the existing zero_charge_no_model_artifacts -> unused_dev_iteration -> release_unused() seam refund the reserved retry slot, with no new counters. log_agent_result() marks the line 'never ran'; the sprint RCA gains an agent_killed_before_output class positioned beneath the shared-infrastructure report #2807 produces. Also fixed a latent gap a negative test caught: a watchdog kill landing exactly on the deadline was not recorded as a timeout (the elapsed fallback only fires past 105% of the limit) and would have been refunded a retry it genuinely spent.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An agent invocation is not terminated by cleanup belonging to work that preceded it. Whatever a prior iteration leaves running is the prior iteration's to reap, and reaping it does not reach a process started afterwards.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Met by evidence plus new regression coverage rather than by a code change, because investigation showed the property already held and the observed kills had a different cause. Traced every signalling path (process-group teardown, direct-descendant cleanup, lease-holder sweep, timeout, stuck-detection, cancellation, orphan reaper, live-story reclaim). Teardown is synchronous in a finally, and the run log confirms iteration 1's teardown completed at 14:38:42, 2m38s before iteration 2 started at 14:41:20. The escapee line at 14:41:31 is iteration 2's own teardown reporting its own descendants after its death. lease_holders() matches an exact per-spawn token, so a later invocation is never a target even though _lease_candidates' window has no upper bound. TestCleanupCannotReachTheNextInvocation now holds that predicate to the claim: A's sweep kills A's escapee and leaves a later-started, later-leased process running.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Where an invocation is nevertheless killed by the system rather than by its own failure, that is distinguishable in the record from an agent that ran and produced nothing.
acceptance_criteria.notes: New failure_code killed_before_output, distinct from agent_ended_without_result. Distinguishable in three places: the operator log line gains 'never ran (killed before any output)'; classify_failure_category returns CATEGORY_PROCESS rather than CATEGORY_NO_RESULT; and the audit's agent_invocation.infrastructure_failure.failure_code carries the code (asserted against real generate_audit_log output). The sprint RCA names it agent_killed_before_output without displacing the shared-infrastructure primary class the spec calls correct. Boundary asserted from both sides: one streamed line keeps agent_ended_without_result, an empty stream gets the new code.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: It does not consume the story's retry budget — a retry that never executed is not evidence about the story, and spending an allowance on it converts an infrastructure fault into an exhausted story.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Achieved by having the runner record a measured cost_usd=0.0 rather than cost-unknown, which was the field blocking zero_charge_no_model_artifacts. No new accounting path. Verified at both halves of the seam: _run_dev_phase reports unused_dev_iteration=True in the exact observed arrangement (prior iteration committed, this iteration zero-output, reaching _left_no_observable_work by its second disjunct as the run log's 'left the preserved branch unchanged' proves), and run_task end-to-end leaves budget.total_count==0 with the full allowance intact. Contrast cases assert no release for a cost-unknown invocation, a pooled transport exception (exit_code=-1), a timeout, or a signal kill that streamed usage.

story_deviations: AC-1 was met by evidence and new tests rather than by a behaviour change. The spec's expected behaviour implies prior-iteration cleanup was reaching the next invocation; the run artifacts show it was not, and the real mechanism is the runner's own post-stream exit-grace SIGKILL. Changing the ownership predicate would have been a fix to a non-defect while leaving the actual cause live. Flagging explicitly since the plan instructed that if investigation resolved the path differently, it be recorded rather than silently claimed.

The plan's Step 2 anticipated a possible audit schema-version bump. None was needed: failure_code already flows to the audit through existing fields, so the persisted shape is unchanged and no migration or schema-guard update applies.

Plan Steps 2/5 named tests/test_runners_cli.py and tests/test_agent_failure.py, which do not exist (both reviewers flagged this). Retargeted to the real homes: tests/test_runner_claude.py, tests/test_agent_ended_without_result.py, tests/test_coord_no_judgment_seam.py, tests/test_process_group.py.

Corrected the prior iteration's uncommitted work, which assumed an external/unowned signal. It gated on a runner_owned_kill flag that would have excluded this very bug from classification, and crashed on a None dereference of extracted_output the first time the branch executed. Both were fixed and the semantics re-grounded on zero execution artifacts.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 correctly identifies unused_dev_iteration as the seam but does not account for the condition that currently gates it. The only production site setting unused_dev_iteration (coordinator/dev_phase.py:2042-2089) sits inside the _left_no_observable_work branch (dev_phase.py:2030-2034), which requires not _has_branch_commits or _changed_since_start is False. The observed failure is iter=2 following a successful iter=1 that cost $1.859 and committed, so the branch will likely be False and the release will never be reached even with a correct classification. Separately, zero_charge_no_model_artifacts() itself returns False when cost_usd is None and when failure_code is in _MODEL_EXECUTION_FAILURE_CODES (agent_failure.py:234-253), so the classified kill must be shown to survive those predicates.
  Suggestion: Before wiring the classification, have the dev trace whether a mid-story supervisor-killed iteration actually reaches dev_phase.py:2030's _left_no_observable_work branch. If it does not, extend the release decision to the classification itself rather than assuming the existing branch carries it, and assert exactly that shape (prior commits present, this iteration zero-output) in tests/test_coord_dev_phase_budget.py.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 1 (root cause unconfirmed; the diagnose-path occurrence may use a different mechanism). Step 1 enumerates the signalling surface and makes confirmation a prerequisite, and Step 4 replaces the synthetic lease-marker test with the real sequential transition, so the risk is bounded rather than open — but AC-1's fix cannot be named until that investigation lands, and the spec's fourth occurrence (forge diagnose runs 431dfd5c8643 / a7b1dffca825, CLAUDE_STREAM_NO_TEXT: reason=missing_result_event) may not share a mechanism with the post-gate DEV kills.
  Suggestion: Keep the plan's own instruction binding: if the diagnose path resolves to a different mechanism, record that in the story explicitly and scope AC-1 to the proven path rather than silently claiming coverage. Note that lease_holders() (process_group.py:297) matches on the per-spawn token from open_process_lease(), so a later invocation carries a different token — the dev should not assume the lease sweep is the killer without evidence from the run artifacts.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Two test files named with Action: modify do not exist: tests/test_runners_cli.py and tests/test_agent_failure.py. The repo's actual homes are tests/test_runner_claude.py, tests/test_runner_codex.py, tests/test_runner_gemini.py, tests/test_runner_providers.py and tests/test_runner_stuck_detection.py for the runner layer, and tests/test_coord_no_judgment_seam.py for agent_failure classification.
  Suggestion: Either create the new files deliberately or retarget to the existing per-runner and no-judgment-seam modules so the new lifecycle assertions land beside the coverage they extend.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 3 (broad exit=-9 exemption) is retired by Steps 2 and 3 — the discriminator is the runner classification with runner-owned timeout/stuck/cancellation excluded and execution artifacts required absent, which matches the existing predicate set in zero_charge_no_model_artifacts(). One concrete case to keep in view: runners/cli.py:903-910 synthesises AgentResult(exit_code=-1, output='ERROR: …') for pooled transport exceptions, so that path must classify as runner-owned rather than falling into the unowned bucket.

plan_finding_registry.description: The plan's first stated risk is carried and threatens the first criterion. Step 1 treats the lower-bound-only _lease_candidates() scan in process_group.py as the likely cross-invocation killer, but lease_holders() also requires the unique token minted by open_process_lease(), and a later invocation receives a different token. _release_group() is likewise bounded to the releasing pgid. The observed kill_escapees() message is emitted after an invocation leader has died and reports cleanup of that invocation's descendants; it does not show that cleanup killed the leader. With the root cause still unconfirmed, the proposed upper bound and Step 4's similar-lease-marker test can pass without resolving the reported termination.

Step 2 uses the wrong API and callers. ProcessTeardown records work left behind after an invocation returns; it cannot prove who terminated that invocation. A system-killed invocation with no surviving descendants can have process_teardown=None, while an agent that fails on its own and leaves children can have a populated teardown. coordinator/dev_verification.py supervises delegated verification commands, not the main DEV agent. Main AgentResult objects are constructed in runners/runner_claude.py, runner_codex.py, and runner_gemini.py, displayed by runners/cli.py, and classified by coordinator/agent_failure.py. Those required callers are absent from the plan.

The plan's second stated risk is carried and Step 3 targets the wrong subsystem. Per-story DEV retry consumption occurs through state.budget.consume() and release_unused() in coordinator/engine.py; coordinator/dev_phase.py derives unused_dev_iteration using zero_charge_no_model_artifacts(). sprint/story_executions.py only records cross-run story ownership and contains no retry accounting. A sprint-boundary test cannot verify or change the coordinator's per-cycle RetryBudget mutation.

The plan's third stated risk is also carried. Exit -9 plus zero output, zero cost, or a ProcessTeardown does not prove supervisor ownership; using that combination can exempt a genuine agent-side signal failure, while missing a system kill that left no descendants. Therefore the proposed guard does not safely retire the overly broad exemption risk on the second and third criteria.

Step 1 proposes adding fields to ProcessTeardown.to_audit_dict(), but that shape is pinned in tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py for both cost.agents and iterations.gate_process_teardowns. The plan omits the required audit schema-version, migration-helper, and snapshot updates, so that change would predictably fail the schema guard.

Step 2's target files do not contain the DEV result path. The '[DEV] FAIL | exit=-9 | cost=$0.000 | output=0 chars' line quoted in the spec is emitted by log_agent_result() at src/theforge/runners/cli.py:930, operating on the AgentResult produced by the runner layer. src/theforge/coordinator/dev_verification.py is the DevVerificationBroker that executes dev-requested verification commands (VerificationRequestRecord, poll_once, _execute) — it has no role in converting an agent CLI invocation into a DEV phase record. src/theforge/sprint/runner.py runs stories/DAG and does not build AgentResult either. A dev agent following Step 2 as written would either wire the teardown marker into an unrelated broker or invent a parallel result path.

Step 3's target files do not own retry accounting, and the plan misses the seam that already exists for exactly this case. The story retry allowance is RetryBudget (src/theforge/coordinator/retry_budget.py), held as state.budget in CoordinatorState (src/theforge/coordinator/state.py); the only mutation site for a dev iteration is state.budget.consume(review_cycle=...) at src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py:760, and RetryBudget already exposes release_unused()/refund() ('Undo the most recent consume() when that reserved slot was never used', retry_budget.py:56-61), already used at engine.py:781-783 via escalation.unused_dev_iteration. src/theforge/sprint/story_executions.py is a crash-detection registry (register_story_execution/scan_story_executions/sweep_story_executions) with no retry state at all, and sprint/runner.py has no per-story dev-iteration counter. Step 3 as written cannot decrement-guard a counter that lives in a module it never opens, and its own stated risk about 'parallel counters' is what it would produce.

Step 5's test targets follow the same misdirection and would not exercise the changed behaviour. tests/test_sprint_runner.py and tests/test_sprint_audit_publish.py sit at the sprint boundary, while the retry-consumption decision and the DEV result rendering both live below it. The repo already has the right-altitude homes: tests/test_retry_budget.py, tests/test_coord_dev_phase_budget.py. As written, criterion 2 and criterion 3 have no test that would fail if the fix regressed.

Carried risk (plan risk 1): the root cause is unconfirmed and the spec itself records a fourth occurrence on a different path — forge diagnose runs 431dfd5c8643 and a7b1dffca825 ending in CLAUDE_STREAM_NO_TEXT / no result event — which the lease-sweep ownership guard in Step 1 would not touch. Step 1 enumerates the process_group.py teardown surface and Step 4 tests the ownership predicate, so the risk is bounded rather than open-ended, but coverage of AC-1 rests on the ownership hypothesis being the operative path.

Plan risk 3 (a too-broad exit=-9 exemption hiding real agent failures) is retired by Step 3's own mitigation — the bypass is gated on the structured supervision marker plus zero output and zero priceable usage — but note that runners/cli.py already synthesises AgentResult(exit_code=-1) for transport exceptions with non-empty output, so the guard must key on the teardown marker rather than on the exit code alone.

Step 1 proposes extending ProcessTeardown.to_audit_dict with new fields. Since the codebase includes tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py, you will likely need to update the pinned audit JSON schemas to explicitly allow or expect these new fields, otherwise the schema validation tests will fail.

Carried risk 1 (root cause unconfirmed; the diagnose-path occurrence may use a different mechanism). Step 1 enumerates the signalling surface and makes confirmation a prerequisite, and Step 4 replaces the synthetic lease-marker test with the real sequential transition, so the risk is bounded rather than open — but AC-1's fix cannot be named until that investigation lands, and the spec's fourth occurrence (forge diagnose runs 431dfd5c8643 / a7b1dffca825, CLAUDE_STREAM_NO_TEXT: reason=missing_result_event) may not share a mechanism with the post-gate DEV kills.

Two test files named with Action: modify do not exist: tests/test_runners_cli.py and tests/test_agent_failure.py. The repo's actual homes are tests/test_runner_claude.py, tests/test_runner_codex.py, tests/test_runner_gemini.py, tests/test_runner_providers.py and tests/test_runner_stuck_detection.py for the runner layer, and tests/test_coord_no_judgment_seam.py for agent_failure classification.
The files tests/test_agent_failure.py and tests/test_runners_cli.py proposed in Step 5 do not exist in the codebase.

Step 2 targets src/theforge/coordinator/audit_substrate.py for the schema version and migration helpers, but CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION and MIGRATION_HELPERS are actually implemented in src/theforge/coordinator/audit_storage.py.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: First confirm the actual signal origin in the gate-failure-to-next-invocation sequence, then fix the responsible supervision path instead of assuming lease-sweep ownership is the cause. Carry an explicit runner termination classification on AgentResult, populated at the CLI runner layer, through coordinator failure classification and DEV budget accounting so non-executed system kills are audited distinctly and release the reserved retry slot.

steps.description: Confirm signal origin and bound cleanup by proven ownership path
steps.details: Make signal-origin investigation an explicit prerequisite before changing the ownership predicate. Enumerate every path capable of signalling the agent leader: process-group teardown, direct descendant cleanup, lease-holder cleanup, timeout kills, stuck-detection kills, cancellation, and any sidecar/reaper path. Reproduce or instrument the real sequential transition of gate failure followed immediately by a new DEV/diagnose invocation. Confirm whether run 0b14b21993ac reached pids [27400, 27402, 27403] through _lease_candidates()/lease_holders(), group membership, or another runner-owned path, and record if the diagnose-path CLAUDE_STREAM_NO_TEXT occurrence uses a different mechanism. Only after that confirmation, add the narrow ownership guard needed for the proven path so cleanup for invocation A cannot signal invocation B while preserving cleanup of A-owned descendants/escapees.

steps.description: Expose runner-owned and unowned termination on AgentResult
steps.details: Define a structured termination classification on AgentResult and populate it in every CLI runner, where runner-owned timeout, stuck-detection, cancellation, transport exceptions, and otherwise unowned negative exits can be distinguished. Do not use ProcessTeardown as proof that the invocation leader was killed; teardown only describes leftover work after an invocation returns. Render the new classification in log_agent_result() so the '[DEV] FAIL | exit=... | cost=... | output=...' line distinguishes a supervisor/system non-execution from an agent that ran and exited -9 with empty output. Plumb the field through AgentResult audit projection and coordinator/agent_failure.py. If the persisted audit shape changes, update the audit schema version, migration helper/fixture, and schema-guard expectations in the same change.

steps.description: Release retry slots for classified non-executed system kills
steps.details: Retarget retry accounting to the coordinator owner. Route the AgentResult termination classification through coordinator/agent_failure.py and coordinator/dev_phase.py so a DEV result classified as an unowned system kill before execution is treated like an unused DEV iteration. Use the existing state.budget.consume(...), escalation.unused_dev_iteration, and release_unused()/refund() path in coordinator/engine.py instead of adding parallel counters. The discriminator must be the explicit runner classification, not exit_code alone; require zero output and zero priceable usage and no stream/session/handoff/structured-data/tool trace before releasing the reserved slot. Keep the shared-infrastructure failure report and audit entry.

steps.description: Add regression coverage for the real sequential invocation transition
steps.details: Replace the similar-lease-marker-only regression with a test that exercises the actual sequential transition: invocation A leaves background work or reaches gate-failure teardown, invocation B starts immediately after, and A cleanup cannot signal B's leader. Add lower-level coverage for the confirmed ownership predicate only after step 1 identifies it. Keep any lease-candidate test focused on the real bug path rather than proving an unrelated upper-bound guard.

steps.description: Add runner, audit, and coordinator budget regressions
steps.details: Cover each runner with fake-CLI lifecycle tests showing timeout/stuck/cancellation kills are runner-owned, transport exceptions keep their existing non-supervisor shape, and an otherwise unowned negative exit with no execution artifacts is classified as a non-executed system failure. Assert log_agent_result() and AgentResult audit projection expose the distinction. At the coordinator DEV-to-engine seam, assert consume() is released via unused_dev_iteration/release_unused() for the classified zero-output, zero-usage system kill, and is not released for ordinary agent failures or exit=-9 alone.

criteria_mapping.criterion: An agent invocation is not terminated by cleanup belonging to work that preceded it.
Where an invocation is nevertheless killed by the system rather than by its own failure, that is distinguishable in the record from an agent that ran and produced nothing.
A retry that never executed does not consume the story's retry budget.

risks.description: The confirmed root cause is not yet identified, and the diagnose-path occurrence may use a different mechanism than the post-gate DEV failures.
risks.mitigation: Treat signal-origin investigation as step 1's prerequisite, instrument the real sequential invocation transition, and only patch the path proven capable of signalling the fresh leader. If diagnose uses a distinct mechanism, record and classify it explicitly instead of assuming the process_group lease fix covers it.

risks.description: Retry accounting is easy to fix at the wrong layer because sprint-level story execution records do not own DEV retry budget.
risks.mitigation: Make the change at coordinator/engine.py, coordinator/dev_phase.py, and RetryBudget's existing release_unused()/refund() seam, with tests in test_coord_dev_phase_budget.py and test_retry_budget.py.

risks.description: A broad exit=-9 exemption could hide real agent-side signal failures.
risks.mitigation: Never key the exemption on exit_code, output length, cost, or ProcessTeardown alone. Require explicit AgentResult termination classification from the runner layer, exclude known runner-owned timeout/stuck/cancellation paths, and require absence of execution artifacts before releasing retry budget.

plan.approach: Finish the process-supervision investigation in the existing process group path, then make teardown ownership bounded by invocation identity and time so one invocation can only reap its own descendants/escapees. Thread the resulting system-kill signal into sprint story accounting so zero-output supervisor kills are audited separately and do not spend retry budget.

steps.details: Audit run_in_process_group(), release_group_record(), _release_group(), kill_escapees(), lease_holders(), and _lease_candidates(). Add an invocation-scoped upper bound or identity guard to escapee discovery so teardown for an earlier invocation cannot match processes started after that invocation's cleanup begins; preserve direct cleanup of children/survivors owned by the releasing invocation. Extend ProcessTeardown/to_audit_dict with enough structured fields to show when cleanup killed supervised processes versus found no owned work.

steps.description: Expose supervisor-caused invocation termination to coordinator results
steps.details: Locate the code that converts agent CLI execution into DEV phase records and the '[DEV] FAIL | exit=... | cost=... | output=...' display/audit line. Plumb the process teardown/system-termination marker from process_group.py into that result path so an invocation killed by supervision is recorded distinctly from an agent process that exited -9 after running with empty output.

steps.description: Prevent non-executed supervisor kills from consuming retry allowance
steps.details: Find the story iteration/retry accounting site and gate retry consumption on the result classification added in step 2. Treat supervisor-killed, zero-output, zero-cost invocations as shared infrastructure failures for story budget purposes: record them audibly, keep the existing failure report behavior, but do not decrement the story retry allowance or mark the attempt as evidence about the story.

steps.description: Add regression coverage for ownership-bounded cleanup
steps.details: Add a focused test around release_group_record()/kill_escapees() using controlled subprocesses or fakes already used in this test module. Cover that cleanup for invocation A kills only A-owned survivors/escapees and ignores a later process carrying similar lease markers that starts after A's teardown boundary.

steps.description: Add sprint-level regression coverage for retry accounting and audit classification
steps.details: Add or extend seam-level tests at the sprint/coordinator boundary to simulate a DEV result classified as supervisor/system-killed before producing output. Assert the record is distinguishable in audit/display data and that the story retry allowance is not consumed. Keep new sprint-wide state on SprintExecutionState or SprintRunContext per project conventions.
